source.title: Scale-invariant Bayesian Neural Networks with Connectivity Tangent Kernel
source.authors: Sungyub Kim; Si-hun Park; Kyungsu Kim; Eunho Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Measures correlations between sharpness measures and generalization gap across trained CIFAR-10 models, using a different model sweep and correlation analysis from the claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates sharpness measures against generalization gap, which bears on V7. Its other classification and calibration results do not test the listed versions. Table 2 reports aggregate and per-hyperparameter correlations; the paper states that 200 of 243 trained models were used. No random-label memorization, width-beyond-interpolation, architecture comparison, optimizer comparison, batch-size effect on test error, dropout effect, or memorized-example removal is tested.
record.test_reason: Table 2 directly tests sharpness–generalization-gap correlations in 200 VGG-based CIFAR-10 models with above 99% training accuracy. It includes Jiang et al.'s magnitude-aware measures and alternative magnitude-aware proxies, including Connectivity Sharpness (CS). This is a different, augmented-data setting from V7's original experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 4.1's empirical conclusion: CS has the highest aggregate correlation statistics among the tested measures, with performance varying by hyperparameter. The paper's broader conclusion is that its connectivity-based prior and posterior produce a scale-invariant PAC-Bayes bound and improve Laplace inference under parameter scaling. The empirical correlations do not establish a causal sharpness–generalization relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a VGG-13-based hyperparameter sweep and sharpness-gap correlation analysis; trains with data augmentation and selects models with above 99% training accuracy rather than directly testing the no-augmentation, similarly-low-training-loss setting in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Granulated Kendall correlations vary by hyperparameter; CS is higher than other measures for three of five and competitive for the remaining two.

fits_no_version.finding: Unscaled Hessian, Fisher, NTK, and original sharpness/bound measures have varying correlations with the generalization gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization-gap prediction depends on the definition of the sharpness or complexity measure.

fits_no_version.finding: Connectivity Laplace improves several uncertainty-calibration metrics and is more stable to prior-scale selection than Linearized Laplace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scale-invariant posterior construction can improve Bayesian predictive calibration.

record.problems: The correlation analysis uses 200 of 243 trained configurations; models were filtered to above 99% training accuracy. The reported correlation coefficients have no uncertainty estimates in Table 2. Data augmentation was used, so it does not match V7's no-augmentation setting.
record.rows_left_out: None of the Table 2 values relevant to the reported correlation comparison were omitted; per-hyperparameter comparator values are not separately extracted beyond the CS results because the paper's stated comparison summarizes CS as higher for three of five and competitive for the other two.

untested.parts: Fitting random labels and comparing held-out performance with natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
The direction and size of large-batch held-out performance penalties and their recovery.
Controlled effects of adding or removing dropout on classification error.

SVHN, the no-data-augmentation setting, and broad comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures. Above 99% training accuracy is enforced, but similarly low training loss is not demonstrated. CS is a local sensitivity proxy rather than a direct perturbation-radius measurement.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Aggregate results for the directly relevant original magnitude-aware measures: Sharpness-Mag. Ψ=0.481, K=0.049; Pacbayes-Mag. Ψ=0.538, K=0.376. These quantify their weaker performance beyond τ and are not covered by the declared omission of per-hyperparameter comparator values.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V7. All extracted numerical values match Table 2. The sweep filters 243 configurations to 200 with above 99% training accuracy, uses batch normalization and augmentation, and reports no uncertainty estimates for Table 2. Per-hyperparameter comparator omissions are explicitly declared in rows_left_out. The supplied text does not substantiate the record's ICLR 2022 publication claim.

versions.untested_parts: Widening beyond the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

No SVHN analysis; no experiment described as holding training loss similarly low across networks; data augmentation was used, unlike the version's no-augmentation condition. The paper reports correlation rather than a causal effect.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
